01 / enterprise digital product leadership

Portland.gov and connected digital platforms

More than
one website.

I manage an interconnected portfolio of public and employee digital platforms, working across product strategy, roadmaps, site architecture, governance, shared standards, and delivery across departments. The goal is a coherent, sustainable public service ecosystem—not a pile of independent projects.

Explore Portland.gov ↗

02 / design systems & equitable access

Design systems · accessibility · digital equity

Design is
infrastructure.

Design is where my career began, and it remains fundamental to my work. I help shape shared design patterns and product practices around ADA Title II digital accessibility, equity, and usable public services. Antiracist practice and language access belong in product decisions—not as a final layer of polish.

Explore City accessibility resources ↗

03 / an earlier design chapter

PortlandMaps.com · the first mobile-first design

A whole city
in your pocket.

More than a decade ago, I designed the first mobile-first version of PortlandMaps.com as part of a collaborative City effort. The challenge was bringing complex public mapping and property information to smaller screens. Other teams have continued developing the service, including a major modernization in 2026. This is a design contribution from an earlier generation, not a claim to the current interface.

Visit PortlandMaps today ↗

04 / public participation & service design

Public-process platforms · eCouncil evolution · government transition

From paper
to participation.

One early project began with discovery, workshops, and mapping the experiences of residents and City staff. I designed a digital public-process platform that replaced a paper-based process on both sides of the counter. Its foundations evolved through later systems, including eCouncil. Years later, the work continues in new forms as government changes.

Explore Portland City Council ↗

05 / operating models & product stewardship

Digital Services Playbook · shared practices

Good systems
help teams work.

Much of my work is designing how digital product teams operate across organizational boundaries: shared methods, visible priorities, stewardship, and room for collaboration. I co-created the Digital Services Playbook with my team and continue exploring how to make portfolio dependencies and tradeoffs more visible.

02 / making systems visible

Make the
invisible
visible.

A digital service is never only its interface. People, policies, information, technology, governance, and capacity determine whether it works—and whether it can keep working. I’m exploring ways to map those relationships to inform product decisions.

Civic Systems Atlas

03 / a practice with convictions

Principles have consequences.

These are commitments I bring to product decisions—not a claim that every barrier has been solved.

Accessibility belongs in the product.

ADA Title II digital accessibility affects roadmaps, design systems, content, procurement, testing, and maintenance—not simply a compliance audit at the end. Title II web accessibility ↗

Digital equity and antiracism should change what gets prioritized.

Whose needs shape requirements? Which barriers are considered urgent? Who has the opportunity to influence decisions? I want teams to examine those questions and be accountable to the people affected by their products.

Language access is a distinct responsibility.

Clear and accessible content matters, and so does people's ability to engage across languages. Title VI nondiscrimination and language access are connected to—but distinct from—ADA Title II disability access. Title VI civil rights ↗

A pilot needs a plan for what comes next.

New services need a path to ownership, maintenance, improvement, or retirement. Capacity, governance, and what we choose not to build matter just as much as launch.

Shared standards should make room for teams and people.

Good operating models clarify decisions and responsibilities across silos. They should make collaboration easier without treating every service, community, or team as identical.

04 / the person behind the practice

A designer,
still designing.

I’m Julie Owens, a designer, maker, and Principal Product Manager for Enterprise Digital Platforms at the City of Portland. My work and the City’s websites have evolved together over two decades. It is collaborative, layered, and difficult to pull apart into a neat timeline—which is part of what makes systems interesting to me.

Design is still my way of thinking. I care about accessibility, digital equity, antiracism, and the invisible structures behind decisions. And I care about making things for no reason more official than curiosity. This is not my résumé or a City website.
